title: Affine sections preserve the structure-algebra ring pushout
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be affine, $A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$ the structure map, and $t_0=f^{-1}\rho$ for $\rho:\mathcal O_X\to A$. Suppose $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$ and $t:f^{-1}A\to B$ form a pushout of $r_0,t_0$ in commutative ring sheaves. For an affine open $V\subseteq X$, set $W=f^{-1}V$, $D=\Gamma(X,V)$, $C=\Gamma(U,W)$, and $\delta=t_W\circ\eta_{A,V}:C\to B(W)$, where $\eta_A$ is the ring inverse-image/direct-image unit. Then the square in commutative rings with both upper maps $f^\sharp_V:D\to C$, lower left map $b_W:C\to B(W)$, and lower right map $\delta:C\to B(W)$ is a pushout.

source.place: Tag 01SB, proof: elucidation and affine reduction; with Schemes Tags 01I9, 01IA and 01HV for affine pullback sections

proof.text: Construct the section tensor ring map q by its universal property. The inverse-image adjunction unit and sheaf pushout equation prove the section square commutes. The resulting q(c tensor d)=b(c)δ(d) formula is proved in Lean.
Use finite product generation to lift any section to the sum of its displayed pure tensors. map_list_sum and the pure-tensor formula prove surjectivity.

Combine the independently stated injectivity with that surjectivity to form RingEquiv.ofBijective. Transport CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct across its categorical isomorphism, using inl_desc and inr_desc for the two section legs.
